sources.title: Evidence scope, probability and diagnostic derivations
sources.details: An identical file hash determines input identity, not task correctness: a constant wrong-answer program has identical bytes across runs. Passing shape/execution tests only verifies those predicates, not an unrelated heldout answer predicate. With p_y>0, NLL=-log(p_y) decreases as correct-answer probability increases. For positive T, z_i>z_j iff z_i/T>z_j/T, so argmax is unchanged; changed wording can retain wrong argmax while T<1 amplifies wrong confidence. SNR=10log10(sum(reference^2)/(sum(error^2)+epsilon)) increases when reconstruction error decreases for fixed reference andmask. For fixed assistantF and transcriptionT, compareF(T(audio)) withF(reference_text): a failure even on reference text is downstream; success only on reference motivates checking transcription. This is a diagnostic control, not universal causal proof. Repeated variants of one shared scene are not independent sampled scenes; their counts must remain subordinate to the parent-family denominator.
